item.title: 'It shouldn't happen to us!' – Denzel Dumfries slams Netherlands after 5-0 Germany thrashing
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-GER-NED - AFP Netherlands captain Denzel Dumfries has described his team's 5-0 defeat to Germany as a collective failure. Dumfries pointed to poor duels and excessive spaces as key factors in the heavy Nations League loss. Heavy loss brings Oranje crashing down The Netherlands wrapped up their UEFA Nations League group stage campaign with a sobering 5-0 defeat against Germany at the Olympiastadion. Having joined Spanish giants Real Madrid in July 2026 following successful spells with PSV and Inter Milan , the experienced right-back captained his country in Berlin as the Oranje were completely overrun in the second half. Despite this heavy 5-0 reverse—marking their biggest defeat of the century and only their second-highest loss against Germany after 1959—Xavi Hernández's side still finished second in Group A2, securing their passage through to the March quarter-finals alongside group winners Germany. Dumfries admits to a poor performance Reflecting on the match in an initial reaction to NOS, Dumfries did not sugar-coat the reality of the performance , identifying glaring structural and physical shortcomings across the pitch. "It was a poor performance. Too weak in the duels and the spaces were too big," Dumfries admitted. "We lost a lot of second balls, we were weak in the duels and they could easily strike on the counter. It was simply a collective failure. That shouldn't happen to us." Frustration boils over on the pitch Dumfries also addressed the mounting tension within the squad during the match, noting that frustration and anger hampered their ability to stay calm and execute their game plan against a ruthless German press. "There is anger and frustration, but in a match like this you have to stay focused," Dumfries noted. "There was also mutual frustration and that is not good." The Dutch inability to close down space allowed players like Florian Wirtz and Brajan Gruda to dictate the tempo, with the opening goal specifically arriving after Dumfries failed to intervene as Derry Scherhant cut inside from the left flank. Regrouping for the quarter-finals While the manner of the defeat stings deeply, the Netherlands must quickly put this disappointment behind them as they look ahead to the Nations League quarter-finals scheduled for March 2027. Dumfries and his teammates will use the winter break to recalibrate, recognising that a repeat of such a collective collapse will not be tolerated when they face Europe's best in the knockout stages.

Trailing 23-20 with just over two minutes left in the fourth quarter at M&T Bank Stadium, Ravens quarterback Jacoby Brissett connected with wide receiver Zay Flowers for a 15-yard gain near midfield. item.title: How MNF win over Ravens impacts Chargers’ No. 1 overall pick chances
item.description: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images How MNF win over Ravens impacts Chargers’ No. 1 overall pick chances appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Chargers finally have something to celebrate after ending their losing streak with a 23-20 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football . The win provided a much-needed boost to their confidence, but it also had an unintended consequence for their draft position. According to ESPN Analytics, the Chargers’ probability of landing the first overall selection dropped from 13% to 7% following their win over the Ravens. This is a six-percentage-point decline, cutting the team’s previous odds by nearly half. There are several games still remaining in the regular season, so the draft order is far from determined. Los Angeles’ performances in the coming weeks, along with the outcomes of other struggling teams, will continue to shape the competition for the top selection. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) However, the win was a big moment for Jim Harbaugh’s squad, marking their first victory in 331 days and ending an 11-game losing streak dating back to last season. Their previous win came on December 21, 2025. With the Ravens’ win, the Chargers became only the second team to win an MNF game after entering with a 0-8 record or worse. The 2013 Tampa Bay Buccaneers were the only other team to achieve the milestone, defeating the Miami Dolphins after starting the season 0-8. Monday’s game also carried a historical distinction, as the Chargers and Ravens entered Monday night with a combined 15 consecutive losses. It set a record for the most combined straight losses by opposing teams heading into a MNF game. As for the Ravens, the three-point loss to a Chargers team that had yet to win a game this season ranks among the most embarrassing blows in team history. It was also just the second time Baltimore had lost to an opponent carrying a 0-8 record or worse. item.title: Ronaldo, Maradona, Baggio - what happened to the World XI?
item.description: [Getty Images] Soren Colding wasn't expecting the call. "The Laudrup brothers, Peter Schmeichel, there might have been some cancellations," he jokes. Eventually, the Danish FA turned to a Brondby defender who had played a handful of times for the national team. The assignment? He would be expected to mark Ronaldo and Gabriel Batistuta as part of a Europe XI against the Rest of the World at Marseille's Velodrome. It was December 1997, and Colding's team-mates would include defenders Fernando Hierro and Alessandro Costacurta, a midfield duo of Zinedine Zidane and Paul Ince, and Patrick Kluivert and Alen Boksic up top. This was a star-sprinkled cast - one player from each of the competing nations at the following summer's World Cup joining forces before the draw took place. "Of course, when you see those names, it was just more or less a dream come true," explains the Dane. Colding was flown to France and chauffeured to the hotel. His driver offered to hang around in case the full-back fancied an impromptu shopping trip. There was no need. Instead, he discovered a bag of Fifa goodies in his room. "There was the biggest Adidas bag I have ever seen in my life," he smiles. "I found a training suit and went down to lunch. "Then I saw all the other guys on round tables - they were sitting with their agents, their wives, their family, their friends in normal [clothes]. Then the Danish guy turned in. Nobody knows who he is, in his Adidas training suit!" Colding struck up a friendship with South Africa defender David Nyathi and the pair where whisked off to a 45-minute training session that afternoon. Not all the big names took part, but one Argentine offered a taste of what was to come. "Batistuta was there and just to see him and his moves, you thought, 'Okay, it's gonna be a nice evening tomorrow'," remembers Colding, who also got to link up with European boss Franz Beckenbauer. "He was pretty cool. He was saying, 'what is your position? Defender? OK, can you play left defender?' No problem - I'll play wherever you place me!" Ronaldo scored twice and assisted three more goals as Rest of the World beat their Europe counterparts 5-2 in Marseille [Getty Images] Come game day, 38,000 fans packed in to see peak Ronaldo. Months earlier, Il Fenomeno completed a world-record move to Inter Milan on the back of 47 goals in 49 games in one sensational season at Barcelona. The 23-year-old was the most exciting player on the planet. "It was crazy, actually," recalls Colding, who previously faced the forward when Denmark's under-21s played Brazil in Florianopolis before the 1996 Olympics. "That was almost the same team as they played with at the World Cup in '98. So we lost 5-1. Just to see his speed and how he played - I played against Roberto Carlos in that game as well - that was just another level. I thought, 'what is going on here?' item.title: Barcelona ready to listen to offers for defensive duo in January – report
item.description: Barcelona ready to listen to offers for defensive duo in January – report Barcelona could sanction the departures of Jules Kounde and Alejandro Balde during the January transfer window as the club looks to generate funds for defensive reinforcements. According to journalist Matteo Moretto on DAZN , the Catalan club is prepared to consider suitable proposals for both defenders, although their futures will also depend on the decisions they make about their playing time. “One or both of them could leave. We’ll see what offers come in and what the players decide,” Moretto said. The possibility of losing two established full-backs would be a significant development for Hansi Flick, particularly with Barcelona also exploring ways to strengthen their defensive options. The club’s financial requirements could therefore force difficult decisions about players who were once important parts of the starting XI. Chelsea emerge as a potential destination for Kounde Kounde’s situation has attracted attention from Chelsea , who are still monitoring his availability ahead of January. Chelsea continue to value Kounde’s versatility. His physical problems have further complicated his efforts to reclaim a regular starting place. It must be remembered that Xabi Alonso’s side attempted to sign Kounde from Sevilla in 2022, but the defender ultimately chose Barcelona. However, with Malo Gusto’s future at Stamford Bridge uncertain, Alonso views Kounde’s ability to operate at both right-back and centre-back as an attractive solution. item.title: Real Madrid superstar achieves remarkable 13-match winning streak in just 50 days
item.description: Real Madrid superstar achieves remarkable 13-match winning streak in just 50 days Real Madrid have enjoyed an extraordinary turnaround under Jose Mourinho in recent weeks, winning eight consecutive matches ahead of the November international break. The Portuguese manager has made some important tactical tweaks that have made such a streak possible. One player in the squad has taken the winning streak to a whole different level, emerging victorious in all 13 matches he has played in the last 50 days. According to MARCA (h/t Madrid Xtra ), Jude Bellingham has not only enjoyed an unbeaten run with his club but has also maintained a perfect record with England. Bellingham celebrates 13 consecutive victories for club and country The 23-year-old’s extraordinary streak began in September. Bellingham has started all eight of Madrid’s games during this period and four of his five games with England. Bellingham has also managed three goals and six assists during this 13-match sequence, continuing his great form in 2026. His latest outing came against Spain on Sunday, when England secured a dramatic 3-2 victory at the Metropolitano . Bellingham delivered another outstanding performance on the night, providing an assist and earning the Man of the Match award. It was a record-breaking assist for the Los Blancos superstar , who reached seven assists for England in 2026, setting a national team record. Mourinho’s midfield leader is back to his best Bellingham’s resurgence is particularly impressive considering the physical difficulties he experienced last season. He missed 111 days through injury, with persistent shoulder problems preventing him from performing at the highest level. How long can Bellingham’s run continue for? (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) He showed signs of returning to his best towards the end of last season before enjoying an outstanding World Cup with England. He now appears to have carried that energy and confidence into Mourinho’s first season back in the Spanish capital. Having Bellingham back to his best is massive news for both the Portuguese manager and Thomas Tuchel. It remains to be seen how long Bellingham’s winning streak can continue and how his form pans out over the course of the season.

The Los Angeles Chargers became the second team since the 2013 Tampa Bay Buccaneers to enter a Monday Night Football matchup with a 0-8 record or worse and come away with a victory. Despite their difficult start to the season, the Chargers finally got things going, defeating the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 on Monday. The much-needed first win clearly meant a lot to linebacker Daiyan Henley, who had nearly been traded to the Denver Broncos. Following the game, Henley expressed his excitement about finally getting the victory. “It’s definitely exciting,” Henley said. “I think you know, everybody was feeding for one, but I think we also know that this feeling is something that we want to keep going, man, so one can lead to two, and we got a short week, so that’s the best part of all of this.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The win carried extra significance for a Chargers team that had struggled to deliver consistent performances on both sides of the ball. The victory brought an end to the Chargers’ eight-game losing streak and finally put their first win of the season on the board. Though one result cannot erase the struggles of their opening eight games, it gives Los Angeles a much-needed starting point to build momentum for the remainder of the season. item.title: Nunes calls for Harrison rematch at featherweight
item.description: Kayla Harrison maintained her perfect UFC record by beating Amanda Nunes [Getty Images] Amanda Nunes has called for a rematch against Kayla Harrison at featherweight after defeat by the UFC bantamweight champion on Saturday. The Brazilian former double champion lost on her return to action after a three-year absence, submitted by American Harrison in the fourth round. Nunes, 38, has a long history with Harrison, having been training partners, and posted on social media she is chasing a rematch at the weight class above. "145 [pounds] rematch," Nunes wrote. "Accepted." Nunes said before UFC 334 she intended to continue fighting even in defeat, while Harrison suggested it could be her last contest in MMA. Harrison,36, had neck and spinal surgery just 10 months ago and has been open about the difficulties of making 135lb (9st 9lb). She said after her win she was considering hanging up her gloves. "I've got a lot of decisions to make when I get home," Harrison said. "Every time I make weight, I say 'never again'. So we'll see." Harrison is unbeaten in her four fights in the UFC and has just one loss on her record, a 2022 loss to Larissa Pacheco in the PFL. Asked if there was any other fight other than the Nunes rematch that would interest her, Harrison said: "If Ronda [Rousey] wants to come get some. It'd be fun. Free money." item.description: There is a changing of the guard in football punditry and the 17th floor of talkSPORT Towers provides a snapshot of its evolution. Listeners, pick your poison. In the morning, you can tune into the veteran of sports broadcasting. Jeff Stelling , once the voice of our Saturday afternoons, hosts your breakfast show alongside Ally McCoist from Mondays through to Wednesdays. It’s classic stuff. While most of his Soccer Saturday colleagues have since been consigned to the scrapheap, Stelling still very much has his foothold in the industry and as such brings us a taste of the ‘good old days’. However, his old-school bread-and-butter style admittedly feels like it’s on its way out, for better or worse. Because in the dark of the night, during the prime-time slot, things go a bit blinky-eyed manic. The seat occupied by Stelling earlier that day is now filled by a man in a mask, shouting into a microphone. Jason Cundy and Jamie O’Hara are changing the pundit’s playbook with The Sports Bar ; it’s chaotic, it’s crude and it does millions. Never one to be behind the times, Stelling recognises the market for football media based largely on mockery nowadays. But don’t expect him to follow suit. Jeff Stelling is an old-school football broadcaster in a changing age (PA Wire) “I think there’s a place for it... not on one of my shows!” Stelling tells The Independent , who will not be showing up to work with a Derek McInnes mask any time soon. “But Cundy and O’Hara, I think at that time of night... it’s irreverent to say the least. Obviously they take the mickey out of each other mercifully, Cundy with his Ange mask and so on. And they take the mickey out of callers as well. I think it works perfectly well at that stage. But you can’t have that all the way through.” Pundits increasingly find themselves leaning into their club loyalties for the sake of entertainment, when purists would argue that the position should be neutral. Stelling, admittedly, was never completely down the middle; he was and still is known for his die-hard fandom of Hartlepool United , where he serves as honorary president. It’s fuelled his love of non-league, which is why he found himself at Woking FC on this grey October afternoon, fronting Enterprise’s Local Legends campaign which strives to celebrate the volunteers that keep clubs like his alive. item.title: Irish boxer Reeves dies aged 31 after three months in coma
item.description: Lee Reeves had been in a coma since his bout with Gary Cully on 1 August [Getty Images] Irish boxer Lee Reeves has died aged 31, three months after he suffered serious injuries in a bout in Dublin, his promoter Queensberry has announced. Reeves was fighting Gary Cully for the vacant BUI Celtic light-welterweight title on 1 August but was knocked out in the 10th round at the 3Arena. The Limerick southpaw was carried out of the ring on a stretcher after the fight and admitted to hospital in a "criticial but stable" condition. He underwent surgery and had been in a ​medically induced coma since. Jonathan O'Brien, Reeves' friend and coach, led tributes, saying he "fought so hard till the end". "Goodbye son, sleep tight, you fought so hard till the end. We love you so much, rest in peace with your mam and brother waiting at the heavenly gates. Look over your sisters and your father, give them the strength to get through this. We love you Lee," O'Brien posted on Instagram. Reeves, who was nicknamed 'El Champo' turned professional in 2018 and he won 16 of his 18 bouts in the ranks. He spent large parts of his early professional career fighting in Canada and Colombia, and impressive performances across the United Kingdom and Ireland led him to face Cully in Dublin in August. Reeves was knocked down twice in the 10th round and was carried out of the ring. Outside of boxing, Reeves - who lost his mum, Cathy, to suicide - was an ambassador for the Limerick Treaty Suicide Prevention group. He also appeared on the BBC reality show Survivor in 2023, which saw contestants stranded on a desert island. 'Limerick in a very dark place' Cully, Reeves' opponent in his last bout, said on Instagram they had known each other for years. "I still remember the stadium days when I used to watch Lee in the nationals, the weight above me, and [I would] always be impressed by his fights and his flashy gear," he said. "What a character and a gent. It's never been nothing but love between us champ, can't really believe I'm writing this but RIP brother." Family friend and Limerick City councillor Catherine Slattery also paid tribute to Reeves: "Limerick is a very dark place tonight with the loss of Lee Reeves. Lee was not just a boxer that excelled in his career - he was a mental health advocate who highlighted mental health and how it can affect young people," she said. "Lee was a very proud Limerick man, he loved Limerick and its people and any chance he got to promote Limerick, he took it. "Lee loved his family. He was very proud of his dad, Tony, and he adored his sisters and his nieces and nephews and they, in return, adored him. "Lee had great faith in God and the only [consolation] is that Lee's mam and brother are embracing him in their arms in heaven. "The loss of Lee will be felt in Limerick for a long time to come and I am heartbroken for Lee that he lost his fight. "Rest in peace El Champ - you will be missed by us all." item.title: Bills Have Chance to Bring Key DB Back After Latest NFL News
item.description: Bills sign Te'Cory Couch. Getty The Buffalo Bills parted ways with a key defensive back this weekend, but could have the chance to bring him back to the practice squad. On Saturday, the Bills announced that versatile defensive back Jordan Hancock had returned from injured reserve and rejoined the active roster. To make room for Hancock’s return, the Bills had to part ways with nickel cornerback Te’Cory Couch, a former practice squad member who earned a call-up to the active roster. The Bills got some good news on Couch on Monday, clearing the way for his potential return. Bills Can Bring Key Player Back to Practice Squad As The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia noted, Couch went unclaimed and now has the chance to pick his next team. That could mean a return to Buffalo’s practice squad. “Former Bills NCB Te’Cory Couch cleared waivers and is a free agent, according to the NFL’s daily transaction log. The Bills waived him on Saturday,” Buscaglia shared in a post on X. Couch appeared in four games this season, playing in 15% of the team’s defensive snaps and 46% of special teams snaps. Couch had been called up twice from the practice squad before being signed to the active roster, so if he does return to the practice squad, he would have just one more elevation. Bills Get Big Debut From Amani Hooker The Bills made a big move for their secondary last week, landing Amani Hooker in a trade with the Tennessee Titans on deadline day. item.title: Body of Melbourne Cup horse found dumped in Sydney skip bin
item.description: So You Are competing in the Melbourne Cup at Flemington Racecourse on 3 November [Getty Images] The body of a top Australian racehorse has been found dumped in a skip bin, hours after its trainer revealed the horse had died from colic. In a video shared online, only two weeks after So You Are raced in the Melbourne Cup, the deceased racehorse appeared to be lying in a large metal bin surrounded by other household rubbish in Sydney. Trainer Bjorn Baker - who shared news of the horse's death from colic on Monday - has said he was "deeply distressed" by the video, and called for a "full explanation". Racing NSW, the state's industry regulator, said a preliminary investigation had found the horse was later properly buried, but called the way its body was handled "completely unacceptable". "Like everyone who has seen the footage, I am deeply distressed by the handling of So You Are's remains," Baker said in an statement shared online. "He was a much-loved horse, and he deserved to be treated with dignity and respect after his death." So You Are had a successful run during spring, winning four times at respected races including the Rosehill, Randwick and the Bendigo Cup. The five-year-old recently finished eight in the Melbourne Cup, which was won by Point of Law, a horse previously owned by King Charles III. The racehorse had received urgent treatment after a severe bout of colic, but was "unfortunately unable to be saved" and was euthanised under anaesthesia, Racing NSW said. "So You Are was then transported for burial, and was being held temporarily, awaiting burial, when these images were recorded," it said. Burial at a licensed landfill is typically recommended for animals that die from euthanasia due to the chemicals involved in the process, according to the racing body. "That burial, however, should have occurred in a timely and respectful manner," it added. In a statement, REC Equine Specialists - the hospital where the horse died - said a contractor had been hired to dispose of the So You Are's body. "We did not carry out the burial ourselves, but we chose the provider and the arrangements, and we take full responsibility for that." "We have spoken with So You Are's owners and trainer to apologise personally." The company added that it had stopped using the contractor, and was reviewing its processes to make sure they known exactly how horses are handled after leaving their hospital. "No owner should have to go through what So You Are's connections have experienced this week. We will make sure it does not happen again." Jowett's video appeared to be filmed at a public rubbish drop-off and land facility called Lucas Heights, in Sutherland Shire, south of Sydney. The waste management company that runs the landfill site said So You Are's body had been moved to a skip bin in a permitted area, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation has reported. Initially, the concern was that MacKinnon had suffered a hip pointer. Nathan MacKinnon Could Be Dealing With More Than a Hip Pointer So, what exactly could be the issue with Nathan MacKinnon? It’s an extremely painful injury that can cause stiffness, limited range of motion, and difficulty moving the affected area. item.title: Messi's Record Crowd Caps MLS's World Cup-Fueled Growth
item.description: Messi's Record Crowd Caps MLS's World Cup-Fueled Growth Lionel Messi scored twice in front of 75,824 fans at Empower Field at Mile High on April 18 — the second-largest crowd in MLS regular-season history. That single Inter Miami road trip to face the Colorado Rapids turned out to be an early signal of what became the league's defining season. By the end of 2026, MLS had posted a 93 percent jump in weekly viewership and its second-highest attendance total ever, with the World Cup running directly through the middle of the calendar. The numbers, released by the league this month, show a sport that didn't just borrow attention from the tournament — it built infrastructure to capture it years in advance. What the 2026 numbers actually show MLS averaged an estimated 7.2 million gross live match viewers per week across streaming and linear platforms in 2026, a 93 percent increase from the previous season. More than 11.2 million fans attended MLS regular-season matches — the second-highest total in league history — at an average of 22,063 per game. Six clubs set single-match attendance records, and three of the ten largest standalone crowds in MLS history came this year. The league also reported a measurable lift in younger viewership specifically tied to the tournament window, with fans skewing toward an average age of 39.6 — younger than any other major North American men's pro league. Should playoff attendance hold, MLS expects to rank among the top three first-division soccer leagues in the world by total attendance for 2026. Why the timing wasn't an accident The bump didn't start when the World Cup kicked off — it was visible before a ball was kicked at the tournament. MLS had already added seven teams and nine soccer-specific stadiums since 2018, rewritten roster rules to push clubs toward investing in young players, and signed a global media partnership with Apple, all explicitly built around the 2026 window. The World Cup itself amplified that groundwork. A record 45 active MLS players appeared across 22 clubs and 17 countries at the tournament — the most of any league in the Western Hemisphere — putting the league's product in front of a global audience mid-season rather than waiting for a traditional offseason bump. What it means for MLS beyond 2026 History is not uniformly kind to host nations. Domestic leagues in South Africa and Brazil saw no lasting attendance boost after their home World Cups in 2010 and 2014. item.description: Messi's MLS Golden Boot Repeat Comes With Brazilian MVP Rivals Lionel Messi has been confirmed as the 2026 MLS Golden Boot winner, becoming the first player in league history to claim the scoring title in back-to-back seasons. He is also a finalist for the Landon Donovan MVP award for an unprecedented third straight year — and this time, two Brazilians stand between him and the trophy. MLS named its year-end award finalists on November 12, with Evander of FC Cincinnati and Guilherme of Houston Dynamo joining Messi, Hany Mukhtar and Cavan Sullivan on the MVP shortlist. Separately, one of Messi's goals from Matchday 28 is nominated for the AT&T MLS Goal of the Year, a fan vote that closed Monday. Why Messi's numbers still separate him Inter Miami CF forward Lionel Messi has won the 2026 MLS Golden Boot presented by Audi, netting 26 goals to become the league's top scorer for the second consecutive season. His 26 goals led the league and made him the first player to win back-to-back MLS Golden Boots, and his 43 goal contributions also led MLS. That consistency is why he remains the favorite for MVP despite the deeper field. Messi scored 26 goals in 31 appearances to claim the 2026 MLS Golden Boot and become the first player in MLS history to win the award in consecutive seasons, contributing a team-leading 17 assists. The nominated goal itself fits the pattern: Messi's near-impossible angle golazo took home the AT&T Goal of the Matchday honor. The Brazilian challenge is new this year What separates 2026 from Messi's previous MVP runs is the company he's keeping. The other four finalists are Evander of FC Cincinnati, Guilherme of Houston Dynamo, Hany Mukhtar of Nashville SC, and Cavan Sullivan of Philadelphia Union — Evander and Guilherme are Brazilian, Mukhtar is German, and Sullivan is American. Guilherme's case is built on a fast adjustment to MLS. item.title: Celtics star Jayson Tatum downplays hand wrap after loss to Magic
item.description: BOSTON — As Boston Celtics wing Paul George spoke to reporters in the locker room on Monday night, star forward Jayson Tatum prepared for his own media availability. But before Tatum went to the podium, Celtics trainer Nick Sang carefully wrapped the six-time All-Star's left hand. Any kind of visible bandage on a team's star player is always a red flag, and Tatum even had his non-shooting hand wrapped up to start the Celtics' showdown with the Orlando Magic . However, he shed the athletic tape early on and went on to log a team-high 24 points in 36 minutes of action during the 115-105 loss at TD Garden. "I bruised my hand last night," Tatum revealed following the double-digit defeat. "So, just tried to wrap it, keep the swelling down a little bit." When asked if the bruise limited his game at all, Tatum shook his head — with his wrapped hand under the press room table — and maintained that he was fine. "Not at all," he replied. Although Tatum was seen grimacing once or twice on the second night of the Celtics' third back-to-back set of the month, the 2024 NBA champion did not have an injury designation coming into the game. Plus, he drained a 3-pointer immediately after one of those winces, perhaps signaling that his bruise was just one of those tame ailments that pops up over the course of an 82-game regular season. Jayson Tatum, who has a wrap on his hand, said he bruised something last night. His response when asked if it impacted his play: “Not at all.” pic.twitter.com/eqnd0UPa6U — Daniel Donabedian (@danield1214) November 17, 2026 Tatum seemed more concerned with Boston dropping its first home game of the 2026-27 campaign than with the material on his hand. The C's trailed the Magic by 9 points at halftime but entered the fourth quarter with a 2-point lead. Yet, in that final frame, Boston was outscored 40-28 and allowed Orlando to shoot over 62 percent from beyond the arc. "For us to come back in the third quarter and then we give up 40 points in the fourth," Tatum began. "We just can't do that again." Despite Monday's late-game woes, the Celtics are 11-3 and in second place in the Eastern Conference. Tatum and company will now prepare for a four-game road trip, which starts Wednesday night with a primetime matchup against the 7-5 Denver Nuggets.
